summary: Today's theme is the double edge of AI investment expectations. The KOSPI plunged 7.57% on foreign selling and a Dell downgrade highlighted memory-cost pressure, while TSMC called AI demand "very strong." Ericsson expects a flat RAN market, and Samsung deepened operator ties around AI-RAN and 6G. Huawei coverage was limited to a single report on ASEAN data centers.

changes.title: KOSPI plunges 7.57% in one day, triggering circuit breakers
changes.why: The KOSPI closed at 5,554.22, its steepest drop since July 28. Foreigners were net sellers of KRW 3.6212 trillion, and reports cited foreign selling and worries about the profitability of AI investment.
changes.impact: With semiconductors weighing heavily in the market, Korean companies' IT investment pace and funding conditions may be affected and warrant continued monitoring.

changes.title: Ericsson sees a flat RAN market; Samsung expands AI-RAN and 6G cooperation
changes.why: Despite 7% organic growth in Q3, Ericsson expects the RAN market to be flat next year. The same day, Samsung published AI RAN and ISAC validation results and continued cooperation with LGU+, KT, SKT and others.
changes.impact: With the overall market not growing, competition is likely to focus on AI-RAN and operator relationships; Huawei should watch Samsung's 6G progress with Korean operators.

changes.title: TSMC: AI demand "very strong", full-year growth raised to about 44%
changes.why: Q3 revenue of US$46.72B (+41.2%) and Q4 guidance of US$52.3–54.3B show AI compute demand backed by results, while gross margin dipped slightly to 66.4%.
changes.impact: Supply-side signals for AI compute are strong, but same-day memory-cost and rating changes show uneven profit distribution, so the cost of Korean AI infrastructure projects should be assessed together.

articles.title: Huawei accelerates hardware supply to ASEAN data centers; Kunpeng chip exports rise
articles.summary: DIGITIMES reported that Huawei is using Singapore as a regional hub to expand server and other hardware deployments in data centers across ASEAN, with Kunpeng chip exports rising. The article is paywalled after the first paragraph, so export volumes, growth rates and share could not be confirmed. It is dated October 14, a day before the collection window, but was included under the extended-search rule as there were no other Huawei items this period.
articles.comment: If accurate, Huawei appears to be expanding its presence in overseas data-center markets with Kunpeng servers; any direct link to the Korean market needs separate confirmation.

articles.title: KT holds "2026 AID-X Day": customer data analysis cut from 8 hours to 10 minutes
articles.summary: KT held a group-wide AX results event at its Pangyo office on October 14–15. Customer feedback analysis was cut from about 8 hours to under 10 minutes and development time from 9 to 6 months (the latter per another outlet). A "maintenance & warranty AX agent pack" built with Tata Daewoo Mobility targets commercial launch in November, aiming to cut manufacturers' warranty costs by 20%, and about 2,000 KT m&s employees saved some 40,000 hours a year using an in-house platform.
articles.comment: The operator appears to be turning internally validated AI agents into B2B products, which could intensify competition in AI solutions for manufacturing.

articles.title: KT signs MOU with KOSHA to spread safety culture at industrial sites
articles.summary: On October 15 at its Gwanghwamun office, KT signed an MOU with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency on spreading safety culture at industrial sites and closing safety gaps. The agreement runs for two years from signing and combines the agency's safety expertise with KT's network infrastructure to support workplace safety management and public safety awareness. Details such as investment size could not be confirmed.
articles.comment: This looks like a new B2B application extending network infrastructure into industrial safety, but its actual scale depends on future disclosures.

articles.title: Ericsson Q3 sales SEK 59.5B, 7% organic growth; RAN market expected flat next year
articles.summary: Ericsson's Q3 net sales were SEK 59.5B (SEK 56.2B a year earlier), with 7% organic growth; Networks grew 9% to SEK 38.7B. Adjusted gross margin was 47.7% and adjusted EBITA SEK 10.1B (17.0% margin; the prior year included a SEK 7.6B capital gain). Management expects a flat RAN market, geopolitical uncertainty and component-cost pressure on gross margin next year, while noting AI features are already improving efficiency in customer networks.
articles.comment: With a flat RAN market, growth must come from share gains and AI/autonomous networks, shifting vendor competition toward operational efficiency and software.

articles.title: Samsung hosts Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit, shares AI RAN, X-MIMO and ISAC validation results
articles.summary: Samsung held a partner day in Mountain View on the 14th (local time) and the Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 on the 15th, with Networks Business head President Woojune Kim giving the keynote. Sessions covered AI-native 6G, NTN-based 6G and connecting physical and digital worlds, with demos of AI RAN, X-MIMO, D-MIMO and ISAC and validation results such as 7GHz-band transmission performance and cell-edge user experience. Cooperation extends from LGU+ (ISAC) and Verizon (field validation at a major Dallas sporting event) to 6G research with SoftBank, NTT DOCOMO, KDDI Research, KT and SKT.
articles.comment: Samsung is cementing ties with Korean operators through joint 6G research with LGU+, KT and SKT, which could shape the local 6G and AI-RAN cooperation landscape.

articles.title: Barclays downgrades Dell: enterprise revenue driven more by memory costs than AI transition
articles.summary: According to AI Weekly, Barclays cut Dell to Equal Weight and lowered its target from US$603 to US$574; Dell shares fell 11% on Wednesday, October 14. Barclays said Dell's enterprise revenue is more a function of memory costs than of the shift to enterprise AI. HPE and NetApp were also moved to neutral, and Oracle, HPE and CoreWeave fell together, wiping out an estimated US$80B in market value.
articles.comment: Rising memory prices appear to be sending mixed signals on AI server and storage profits and demand, which may make server vendors more cautious on pricing and delivery.

articles.title: Kakao unveils "AI for Everyone": 34 organizations, year-end launch, 5M MAU target
articles.summary: Kakao unveiled "AI for Everyone" at its if(kakao)26 developer conference on the 14th. The service, available in KakaoTalk and on the web, lets companies and developers participate with specialized agents and tools, handling tasks from exhibition recommendations to restaurant search and booking while reconfirming conditions and amounts before execution. 34 companies and institutions are involved: Kakao handles the service and AI workflows, LG Uplus model and GPU operations, and LG AI Research provides EXAONE. After an October beta, a full launch is planned for year-end targeting 5 million MAU, with "one agent per person" phased in from 2027.
articles.comment: As this national AI project runs on operator GPUs and domestic models, Korea's AI service compute and model stack appears to be consolidating around domestic corporate alliances.

articles.title: Reuters: Anthropic November share sale valuation discussed at US$1.5T; FTC sends demands to OpenAI and Anthropic
articles.summary: According to a Reuters report relayed by AI Weekly, investors are discussing a US$1.5T valuation for a November Anthropic share sale, down from about US$2T earlier. Q3 revenue rose 45% to US$16.8B. The US FTC also sent 50-page civil investigative demands to both OpenAI and Anthropic, focusing on security incidents and safeguards. All of this is relayed from an aggregator page; the original reports could not be confirmed.
articles.comment: Valuations and regulatory pressure on leading model companies are shifting at the same time, which could affect global AI compute investment expectations and enterprise adoption choices.

articles.title: NVIDIA releases open-weight Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: 120B parameters, 1M-token context
articles.summary: AI Weekly reported that NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL as an open-weight model. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 120B total and 12B active parameters and supports a 1-million-token context. Benchmarks, license and exact release timing are not on the page, so only the specs are confirmed; as the source is an aggregator, it should be rechecked against NVIDIA's official announcement.
articles.comment: NVIDIA appears to be using open models to anchor its hardware ecosystem, which could deepen sovereign AI projects' reliance on the NVIDIA stack.

articles.title: KOSPI closes at 5,554 after 7.57% plunge; circuit breakers in both markets, foreigners net sell KRW 3.6T
articles.summary: On October 15 the KOSPI fell 454.59 points (7.57%) to 5,554.22 and the KOSDAQ dropped 7.65% to 760.82; the intraday low was 5,450.81 (-9.29%). Level-1 circuit breakers were triggered on both the KOSPI and KOSDAQ (KOSPI at 12:38), the steepest drop since July 28 (-10.84%). Foreigners net sold KRW 3.6212T while institutions (KRW 1.6907T) and individuals (KRW 1.2880T) were net buyers; reports cited foreign selling and AI investment profitability concerns. Per the Korea Economic Daily, foreign net selling before the plunge was about KRW 93T, with foreign ownership at 38.65%.
articles.comment: Korea's semiconductor-heavy stock market appears highly sensitive to AI investment sentiment, which could affect corporate IT investment and funding conditions.

articles.title: CXMT pledges 4F² server DRAM this year, pressuring Samsung and SK hynix shares
articles.summary: CXMT said it will release server DDR5 RDIMMs with a 4F² cell structure by year-end. This theoretically shrinks cell area by about 33% versus 6F², but capacity, speed, volumes and customers were not disclosed. Without EUV, repeated multi-patterning makes yield and cost key variables, and brokers see a 5–7 year mass-production gap with Samsung. On the 13th, Samsung and SK hynix shares fell 7.39% and 10.09%, respectively; CXMT's monthly capacity is about 350,000 wafers by year-end, with roughly 9.5% DRAM share in Q2 (TrendForce).
articles.comment: The pace of catch-up and capacity expansion, more than the technology itself, appears to be unsettling market expectations; memory prices and supply dynamics warrant monitoring.

articles.title: TSMC Q3 revenue US$46.72B (+41.2%): AI demand "very strong", full-year growth raised to about 44%
articles.summary: TSMC's Q3 revenue was US$46.72B, up 41.2% year over year and 16.2% quarter over quarter, above guidance. HPC accounted for 68% and gross margin was 66.4%, down 130bp from the prior quarter. Q4 revenue guidance is US$52.3–54.3B, full-year US-dollar revenue growth about 44%, and this year's capex US$60–64B. CEO C.C. Wei said AI-related demand is very strong and actual demand may exceed earlier assumptions.
articles.comment: AI demand is confirmed by results but margins are under pressure, so profit distribution and cost pressure across the compute supply chain need continued watching.

analysis.title: The AI server profitability debate: memory costs, Dell downgrade and CXMT 4F²
analysis.facts: Barclays cut Dell to Equal Weight, saying enterprise revenue reflects memory costs; HPE and NetApp were also adjusted, and Oracle, HPE and CoreWeave fell. CXMT pledged 4F² server DRAM this year. The same day, TSMC said AI demand is very strong.
analysis.why: Strong AI demand does not necessarily mean strong server-vendor profits. Rising memory prices may shift profits to memory makers, while new suppliers make the price outlook uncertain.
analysis.impact: Server and storage quotes and lead times for Korean AI data-center projects may be affected by memory prices, so the cost structure of AI compute solutions needs to be reassessed.
analysis.watch: Earnings guidance from Dell and other server vendors · CXMT 4F² DRAM actual shipments and yields · Memory contract price trends

judgments: AI demand is backed by results (TSMC), but capital-market doubts about profitability are showing up in the KOSPI and server-vendor stocks, so investment pace may diverge further.

With the RAN market entering a flat phase, vendor competition is shifting to AI-RAN, 6G and operator relationships, and AI and general compute demand is likely to come more from operators' data centers and networks.

As Korean AI projects such as "AI for Everyone" rely on domestic operators' GPUs and models, Huawei's entry points in Korea are more likely to be networking, optical transport and data-center peripheral solutions than a full AI platform.
watch: Whether the KOSPI stabilizes, foreign flows, and spillover into corporate IT budgets.
Results of KT's union vote on the 15th and LG Uplus's 12th round of negotiations (not confirmed this period).
Progress of the "AI for Everyone" October beta and LG Uplus's role in GPU operations.
Anthropic IPO valuation and FTC investigation progress (relayed by an aggregator; original reports need confirmation).
Scale of Huawei's Kunpeng and data-center deployments in ASEAN, and new moves in Korea.
